name: accordion
title: Accordion
description: A vertically stacked set of interactive headings that each reveal a section of content.

props.name: collapsible
props.description: Whether an accordion item can be closed after it has been expanded.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description:
The initial value of the expanded accordion items.
Use when you don't need to control the value of the accordion.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the accordion items are disabled

props.name: getRootNode
props.description: A root node to correctly resolve document in custom environments. E.x.: Iframes, Electron.

props.name: ids
props.description: The ids of the elements in the accordion. Useful for composition.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Whether multiple accordion items can be expanded at the same time.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The orientation of the accordion items.

props.name: value
props.description: The controlled value of the expanded accordion items.

events.name: onFocusChange
events.description: The callback fired when the focused accordion item changes.

events.name: onValueChange
events.description: The callback fired when the state of expanded/collapsed accordion items changes.

keyboard.description: Moves focus to the next/previous focusable trigger.
Toggles the focused item's expanded state.
Moves focus to the next trigger, looping to the first.
Moves focus to the previous trigger, looping to the last.
Moves focus to the first trigger.
Moves focus to the last trigger.

accessibilityNotes: Full keyboard navigation is supported, adhering to the WAI-ARIA Accordion design pattern.
Each trigger is a real `<button>` inside an `<h3>`, so it participates in the page's heading outline.

examples.title: Default
examples.description: A single item at a time can be open. Pass `collapsible` to allow closing the open item.

examples.title: Basic
examples.description: A basic accordion that shows one item at a time, open by default.

examples.title: Multiple
examples.description: Pass `multiple` to allow more than one item to be open at the same time.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.description: Pass `disabled` to disable every trigger in the accordion.

examples.title: Borders
examples.description: Add a border between items with a descendant selector on the root class.

examples.title: Card
examples.description: Wrap the Accordion in a Card component.

examples.title: RTL
examples.description: Accordion restyles correctly under `dir="rtl"` with no component changes.

examples.title: Not collapsible
examples.description: Without `collapsible`, the open item cannot be closed by clicking its own trigger.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.description: Zag machines are controlled: a `value` prop without a change handler never moves. Pair it with `valueChange`.

examples.title: Compound (attr tags)
examples.source:
import Accordion from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/accordion/accordion.marko";

<Accordion collapsible defaultValue=["item-1"] class="w-full max-w-md">
  <@item value="item-1" title="Is it accessible?">
    Yes. It adheres to the WAI-ARIA design pattern.
  </@item>
  <@item value="item-2" title="Is it styled?">
    Yes. It comes with default styles that match the other components' aesthetic.
  </@item>
  <@item value="item-3" title="Is it animated?">
    Yes. It's animated by default, but you can disable it if you prefer.
  </@item>
</Accordion>
examples.description: Use `<@item>` attribute tags instead of `items=` to compose each item's title and content directly in markup.

composition:
Accordion renders its own item/trigger/content anatomy internally — there
are no separate AccordionItem/AccordionTrigger/AccordionContent tags to
compose. Choose one of two equivalent forms:

```text
Accordion (items=)
├── item 1 { value, title, content }
├── item 2 { value, title, content }
└── item 3 { value, title, content }
```

```text
Accordion
├── <@item value title>content</@item>
├── <@item value title>content</@item>
└── <@item value title>content</@item>
```

Both sources are merged into one normalized item list before rendering, so
they may be mixed across an app but not within a single Accordion instance
(attr tags win if both are present on the same tag).
